info.text:
# Wedding Witch

## What does randomization do to this game?

The witch's meta-upgrade shop stops selling upgrades. All 73 of its purchasable levels
become Archipelago items, so the only permanent power the witch has is what the
multiworld sends her; the shop's shelves are restocked with Archipelago checks, which
is what Love Coins buy instead. Your upgrade levels still show in the panel below the
stock, unbuyable.

Which difficulties you can play is also the multiworld's to decide, rather than the
game's usual "clear the last one to open the next".

## What is the goal?

Clear the Nightmare Wedding boss in a number of different witch forms — six by
default, settable from 1 to 6 with Goal Forms. The forms are Big Breasts, Small
Breasts, Corruption, Beast, Muscle and Hips, and the one you finish in is decided by
which potion type you levelled, so each is a separate winning run. Winning as the
untransformed witch never counts.

## What items and locations get shuffled?

Locations are:

- **Potions** — drinking one of the three potions offered at the end of a stage. Each
  slot is its own check, so a stage pays out three across as many visits: 54 in all,
  over 5 stages on Normal, 6 on Hard and 7 on Nightmare. Turn off Potion Slot Locations
  for one check per screen instead, and 18 in all.
- **Bosses** — clearing a difficulty's boss. Nightmare splits this six ways, one per
  witch form; Normal and Hard just want it dead in any form, because their shorter runs
  rarely offer enough of one potion type to transform at all. 8 checks.
- **Shop** — buying a shelf in the witch's shop. Shop Locations of them, 20 by
  default.

A default seed is 82 locations: 54 potions, 8 boss clears and 20 shelves.

Collecting Nightmare's six boss forms already takes six runs of it, and six visits to a
stage more than cover its three potion slots — so on the difficulty that matters most,
the slots cost you very little beyond what the forms already ask.

Clearing a stage is not a check in itself. The potion screen it leads to is, so a
cleared stage already pays out once — counting the clear as well would have doubled
every run.

Items are the 17 shop upgrades, each named after the thing itself — a copy of
Witch's Hat raises its level, and it has five. Witch's Bag and Phantasm Mirror have a
single level each. Progressive Difficulty opens Hard and then Nightmare, replacing the
game's own "clear the last one first" unlock.

Whatever is left over is a wedding gift, prefixed `Gift:` — the witch is extorting
lingerie out of the devils, and a gift is worth exactly as much as that suggests. A
default seed has room for 17 of them.

## Which items can be in another player's world?

All of them.

## What does another world's item look like in Wedding Witch?

Nothing appears in the world itself — checks fire the moment you clear a stage, win
as a form, or complete an achievement, and the item goes straight to whoever owns
it.

## Notes

Your upgrade levels, coins and lifetime stats are kept per room. Connecting neither
reads nor writes your normal save.

tutorials.text:
# Wedding Witch Setup Guide

## Required software

- Wedding Witch on Steam
- [BepInEx 6 bleeding edge](https://builds.bepinex.dev/projects/bepinex_be), the
  **Unity.Mono** x64 build
- The Wedding Witch Archipelago mod, from
  [its releases page](https://github.com/chickentuna/WeddingWitchMod/releases/latest) —
  which also carries this world's `.apworld` and a template YAML

## Installing BepInEx

Wedding Witch is a Unity **Mono** build, so it needs the Mono flavour of BepInEx:
`BepInEx-Unity.Mono-win-x64` on Windows, `BepInEx-Unity.Mono-linux-x64` on Linux.
The IL2CPP builds will not load. The mod itself is the same file on both.

Unzip it into the game folder, next to `Wedding Witch.exe` (or
`Wedding Witch.x86_64`), then launch the game once and quit. That first run creates
`BepInEx/plugins`.

On Linux, set the game's Steam launch options to `./run_bepinex.sh %command%`.

## Installing the mod

Unzip the mod into `BepInEx/plugins`, so you end up with
`BepInEx/plugins/WeddingWitchArchipelago/WeddingWitchArchipelago.dll`.

## Connecting

Launch the game. The Archipelago panel opens by itself when there is no session;
press <kbd>F1</kbd> to bring it back. Fill in the server address, port, your slot
name and the room password if there is one, then press Connect.

The details are remembered for next launch, and
`BepInEx/config/com.jpn.weddingwitch.archipelago.cfg` has a `ConnectOnStart` setting
if you would rather skip the panel entirely.

## Playing

The Upgrades shop still opens and still shows your levels, but nothing in it can be
bought — the levels shown are the ones the multiworld has sent you.

Your progress lives with the room, not with your normal save file. Disconnecting and
reconnecting to the same room picks up exactly where you left off; playing
unconnected leaves your ordinary save untouched, though the shop stays closed.

notes.text:
## Changes since 0.1.0

- Achievements pay out their Love Coins again: each room now keeps its own achievement progress instead of sharing your normal save's.
- The main menu's **Shop** button can be reached with the arrow keys and gamepad.

The apworld and YAML are unchanged from 0.1.0, so existing seeds keep working.

Archipelago randomizer for **Wedding Witch**. The witch's upgrade shop stops selling
upgrades — all 73 levels become Archipelago items — and its shelves are restocked with
checks instead, which is what Love Coins buy now.

A default seed is 82 checks: the three potions offered after every stage, the boss beaten
in each of the six witch forms on Nightmare (once in any form on the lower difficulties),
and 20 shop shelves.

## What's in this release

| File | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| `WeddingWitchArchipelago-0.1.1.zip` | unzips into the game folder |
| `wedding_witch.apworld` | your Archipelago install's `custom_worlds/` |
| `WeddingWitch.yaml` | your Archipelago install's `Players/`, after editing |

## 1. Install BepInEx

Wedding Witch is a Unity **Mono** build, so it needs the Mono flavour of BepInEx 6 from
the [bleeding-edge builds page](https://builds.bepinex.dev/projects/bepinex_be). The
IL2CPP builds will not load. Take the newest one for your platform:

- **Windows** — `BepInEx-Unity.Mono-win-x64-6.0.0-be.*.zip`
- **Linux** — `BepInEx-Unity.Mono-linux-x64-6.0.0-be.*.zip`

Unzip it into the game folder — the one holding `Wedding Witch.exe` on Windows or
`Wedding Witch.x86_64` on Linux. Steam's *Manage → Browse local files* will take you
there.

Then launch the game once and quit. That first run creates `BepInEx/plugins`, and it
will not create it until the game has actually started.

**Linux only**, two extra steps:

```sh
chmod +x run_bepinex.sh
```

and set the game's Steam launch options to:

```
./run_bepinex.sh %command%
```

Without the launch options BepInEx is never loaded and the game simply runs unmodded.
Windows needs neither — its BepInEx hooks the executable directly.

## 2. Install the mod

Unzip `WeddingWitchArchipelago-0.1.1.zip` into the same game folder. It carries its own
`BepInEx/plugins/...` path, so you should end up with:

```
Wedding Witch/BepInEx/plugins/WeddingWitchArchipelago/WeddingWitchArchipelago.dll
```

## 3. Install the apworld

Drop `wedding_witch.apworld` into `custom_worlds/` in your Archipelago install, then edit
`WeddingWitch.yaml` and put it in `Players/`. Both the host generating the seed and anyone
tracking it need the apworld.

## 4. Play

Launch the game. The connection panel opens itself on the main menu; <kbd>F1</kbd>
toggles it. Fill in the server address, port, your slot name and the room password if
there is one, then press Connect. Your details are remembered for next launch.

The main menu gains a **Shop** button beside **Upgrades**: Upgrades lists the levels the
multiworld has sent you, unbuyable, and Shop sells Archipelago checks for Love Coins.

Your upgrade levels, coins and stats are kept per room, so connecting neither reads nor
writes the save you play unconnected.

## Notes

Universal Tracker is supported and needs no YAML of its own.

Which difficulties you can play comes from the multiworld rather than from clearing the
previous one, so expect Hard and Nightmare to be locked until the items turn up.
